title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator joins channel meetings
summary: The rollout dates, licensing and published admin paths are supported. The automation gap is too broad: Microsoft documents an operation to unblock a Teams app, even though its examples do not reliably identify the blocking value.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Facilitator can be allowed or blocked in Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for the organisation-wide control that allows or blocks Facilitator.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 2b876f4d-2e6b-4ee7-9b09-8893808c1380 -IsBlocked $false ... Unblocks 1Page App ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to kind 'powershell', call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $false', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp'. In the note, state: 'Automation shown here unblocks the app, as described in reference example 4. The reference also describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking, so a reliable blocking value is not stated; use the admin UI to block.' Keep the tenant-wide UI path unchanged.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app

claims.claim: A reliable blocking value for Update-M365TeamsApp is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Facilitator block app PowerShell Set-TeamsApp Update-M365TeamsApp IsBlocked; Update-M365TeamsApp block true. Read update-m365teamsapp; examples 3 and 4 describe both Boolean values as unblocking, and the parameter text does not map values to blocking.

claims.where: Governance controls: row 1 prose; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Facilitator page describes group availability through app policies and app-centric management.
claims.quote: To allow Facilitator for users, a new app policy needs to be created and then assigned to users. ... You can then assign the policy to your entire tenant or to a select group of users.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: table row 2; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled $false disables collaborative AI-generated meeting notes.
claims.quote: Disable Loop workspace creation and Loop component creation and integration everywhere ... Set-SPOTenant -IsLoopEnabled $false, Set-SPOTenant -IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled $false

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin-centre UI for the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled property.
claims.quote: Searched: IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled admin center UI settings. Read loop-components-configuration and facilitator-teams; their UI controls govern Loop workspaces or Cloud Policy, while this property is documented through SharePoint PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].note and scope; Governance controls: row 2 prose
claims.claim: The collaborative meeting notes property is tenant-wide and cannot be configured per user.
claims.quote: This property controls the collaborative meeting notes creation and integration in Microsoft Teams. It applies to the entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.where: Governance controls: row 2 prose; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Facilitator page says disabling the property turns off AI-generated meeting notes for all users.
claims.quote: if you disable this setting, AI-generated notes for meetings is turned off for all users in your organization.

claims.claim: The property does not apply to collaborative notes in Teams New Calendar, where Cloud Policy applies instead.
claims.quote: The SharePoint organization property doesn't apply to collaborative meeting notes in Teams New Calendar, see Settings management in Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: Managing the property requires the SharePoint PowerShell module.
claims.quote: You'll need the latest version of SharePoint PowerShell module to enable or disable Loop experiences in Teams.

claims.claim: Channel meeting scheduling is under Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting scheduling.
claims.quote: expand Meetings > Meeting policies and choose the policy you want to update. ... Under Meeting scheduling ... toggle Channel meeting scheduling to Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False restricts channel meeting scheduling.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowChannelMeetingScheduling $False

claims.claim: Turning off channel meeting scheduling prevents users from creating new channel meetings.
claims.quote: If this setting is turned off, users can't create new channel meetings

claims.claim: The organiser can still edit existing channel meetings after scheduling is disabled.
claims.quote: but the event organizer can edit existing channel meetings.

claims.claim: Turning off meeting policy settings disables join links for existing meetings of that type previously organised by assigned users.
claims.quote: The meeting join links and conference IDs of all existing meetings of that type that the user previously started or scheduled don't work.

claims.claim: Turning off those settings also disables the existing meetings' conference IDs.
claims.quote: The meeting join links and conference IDs of all existing meetings of that type that the user previously started or scheduled don't work.

claims.claim: Existing meeting content remains retained and accessible after the policy settings are turned off.
claims.quote: The conversations, files, whiteboards, recordings, transcripts, and other content related to the meeting are retained and users can still access them.

claims.claim: Channel meeting scheduling is a per-user policy control.
claims.quote: These settings are per-user policies and they apply before a meeting starts.

claims.claim: Channel meeting scheduling governs scheduling rather than Facilitator inside meetings.
claims.quote: Channel meeting scheduling: Controls whether a user can schedule a meeting in a channel. ... These settings are per-user policies and they apply before a meeting starts.
